# 📦 @goodandready/dsh-opencode-provider
OpenCode Console & OpenCode Go LLM Provider for DeepSeek Harness
⭐ If you like this plugin, please star it on GitHub — it shows me that the plugin is useful to you a
nd motivates me to keep developing it.
🐛 If you find a bug or would like to request a feature, open a GitHub issue in any language — I will
review your proposal and implement useful suggestions in a future plugin version.
OpenCode / OpenCode Go provider plugin for DeepSeek Harness (dsh).
It registers two native LLM routes:
| Route | Product | Base |

| `opencode-direct` | OpenCode Console / Zen (pay-as-you-go) | `https://opencode.ai/inference` |
| `
opencode-go-direct` | OpenCode Go / Go Plus subscription | `https://opencode.ai/inference/go` |
Requests resolve the key per call, so a changed credential reaches the next request without a restar
quests resolve the key per call, so a changed credential reaches the next request without a restart.

The ids use the `-direct` suffix because the built-in `llm-pi-ai` catalog already owns
`opencode` an

d `opencode-go`. Reusing those ids makes the core registry reject the
duplicate (`DUPLICATE_DIRECTOR

Y`) and drop the built-in catalog, which hides the other
providers and disables the add button. Exis

ting sessions recorded under the old ids stay on
the built-in routes; select **OpenCode (plugin)** o

r **OpenCode Go (plugin)** for this
plugin's accounts, quotas, fallback and telemetry.
## Architecture

## What works

- **Four wire transports**, chosen per model:
- OpenAI Chat Completions (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiMo,

LongCat, Hy3, Step, …).
- Anthropic Messages (Claude Haiku, MiniMax, Qwen).
- OpenAI Responses (GPT,

Grok, Muse).
- Google Generative AI (Gemini).
- **Text, reasoning, streamed tool calls, usage, fini

sh reasons.**
- **Images** through the durable attachment service, rendered natively per transport;
**file attachments** are projected to DSH's deterministic handle text (the harness supplies the read

-only execution path), never inline bytes.
- **Tool-result images** are inlined by Anthropic, OpenAI
Responses and Google; OpenAI Chat keeps the text placeholder because its tool message has no image

part.
- **Replay of provider metadata** where the endpoint requires it:
- Anthropic thinking signatu

res.
- Gemini `thoughtSignature` on historical function calls.
- **Multi-account rotation** before a
stream starts: 401/403/429 and quota/usage-limit bodies (400/402/403/429). An invalid key cools dow
n for 24h, a quota rejection for 10 minutes or `Retry-After`, a rate limit for 60s or `Retry-After`.
A request already streaming is never replayed on another account; the next request uses the next us

able key.
- **Per-account quotas**: each account row shows its own 5-hour / weekly / monthly usage,
the active account drives the sidebar and quota panel, and the panel lists every account side by sid

e.
- **Per-account runway**: estimates time to exhaustion from the average burn rate of each window
and marks the first window projected to run out before its reset; approximate because the API expose

s only the current percentage and reset time.
- **Model → account rules**: first matching glob pins

a preferred account for that model; the other accounts remain fallbacks if it fails or is cooling.

## Verified in DSH Desktop
Tested against DSH Desktop **0.2.1-rc.2**:

- the plugin loads and `/dsh-opencode/state` returns `200`;
- the key is picked up from `~/.local/sh

ndows returned `rolling / weekly / monthly`;
- `/dsh-opencode/analytics` scanned 7 local sessions (0

OpenCode sessions yet, as expected before the first OpenCode chat);
- `/dsh-opencode/test` against

the default flash model returned `{"ok":true,"text":"OK"}`;
- a second Go account was added, the def
ault key was temporarily replaced with an invalid one, and `/test` rotated to the second account and

still returned `OK`;

Every field except `apiKey` is volatile and appears in dsh settings.
## Limitations
- File attachments are forwarded as DSH handle text, not inline bytes; the harness normally supplies
the read-only execution path. Tool-result images are inline on Anthropic, OpenAI Responses and Goog

le; OpenAI Chat uses a placeholder.
- The usage endpoint is unofficial and may change; chat never de

pends on it.
- Cost is displayed only by DSH's native cost display; this plugin has no second compos

er cost pill.
- Automatic update requires the DSH CLI entry in the runtime. When it is not exposed,

the update card shows the current/latest status and directs the user to the DSH plugin manager.
- Su
bscription request counts are OpenCode's published estimates, not enforced quotas. They can change w

hen OpenCode updates the Go pricing table; the gateway is the final authority.
- Usage-by-model aggr
egates the local projection cache and attributes a whole session to its last-used model; a session t

hat switched models is therefore approximate. It never reads prompt text or titles.
- `opencode-dire

ct` (Console) billing shows no per-model allowance; the Go route is the primary target.
- The anonym

ous free lane (`Bearer public` + CLI impersonation) is not implemented.
- The UI requires a web prof

ile (the Host needs `ctx.webServer`); the TUI keeps the `/opencode` command and the model routes.
-
Write routes are loopback-only; a web profile exposed to a LAN can read state but cannot save config
uration or keys until the host auth token is integrated.
